messages:
alex: FYI observed host-side p99 jump after the latest runtime roll. Short requests (1-3 tokens) affected most.

maria: confirmed on prod-4. kvcache eviction rate up ~3x on hosts handling many small writes.

chen: quick perf top on a repro node: 

```
$ perf top -p 31789
 13.2%  libgrpc.so          grpc_chttp2_transport_parse
  8.7%  runtime.so          kernel_binner_select
  6.0%  runtime.so          kvcache_evict
  4.4%  libc.so.6           writev
```

alex: looks like header/coalesce changes in grpc are changing observed write boundaries so the binner picks the scalar kernel more often. Scalar kernel + smaller minibatches => less KV reuse.

sam: eBPF stack traces show writev -> grpc_frame_builder -> header_coalesce hotspots. SDK keepalive/settings increases frame churn.

rachel: repro uploaded: many short http2 streams doing 1-token loops. p99 climbs in ~2 minutes.

maria: triage plan: 1) flip header_coalesce=false on a canary host; 2) add smoothing to kernel binner (50ms window); 3) emit minibatch_len histograms (1,2,4,8 buckets at 1% sample); 4) run 30m soak.

chen: I can run perf record + flamegraph and heaptrack on the canary after toggle.

alex: temporary mitigation: increase kvcache bucket size on affected hosts to reduce eviction frequency. Longer term: prefer time-windowed batching for small-write workloads.

sam: I'll schedule rollback for the canary at 23:45 UTC and coordinate with oncall.

rachel: set alert: host.ingress.kv_evictions_per_min > 6 => page. Monitoring pinned to this channel.

maria: action items captured. will land kernel-binner guard behind a flag and test with the soak.

alex: thanks everyone. please post flamegraphs and eBPF outputs here when available.
